response.statement: [re SC10-N1 — answered: same anchor, by construction, now a contract term] K8's paint is driven off `anc.ch10.relay-answer` ITSELF — not off a K7 paint-completion event, and not off a second clock. The contract term, stated for quoting: 'anc.ch10.relay-answer is a single anchor; the answer figure's audio onset and K8's paint-begin both key off it in the same frame — simultaneity by shared anchor, never by tuned offsets.' Your retime option is therefore unneeded; your at-anchor cue relation already satisfies the term. AMENDMENT (the one addition, a guard so a future retune cannot silently break the ordering): the ch10-ask mood's published tempo must satisfy 2 beats ≥ 1.36s (K7's 55-char RELAY reveal at 22 ms/char = 1.21s + 0.15s settle), i.e. tempo ≤ ~88 bpm — automatically satisfied by the shipped TEMPO_MAX 88, but recorded as an explicit inequality in the contract next to the anchor definition. Net effect at 68 bpm: the answer sounds ~1.76s after ask onset, AFTER the request finishes painting and INSIDE the two-bar figure still sounding — text-complete, phrase-incomplete — which is exactly K9's claim and exactly your metric-fact realization. Aligned by construction; the contract will say so. [re SC10-N2 — confirmed, both halves] (a) 'step' tolerates whole-tone precision — in plain speech a step IS a whole step, and your semitone-is-the-dread-interval argument is the intent's no-antagonist law realized in interval choice; K1 freezes as written. (b) No diegetic core hum SFX exists to my knowledge and NONE may be added this run: no SFX surface is in allowedPaths and the audio engine paths are protected. The pitch move lives in exactly one lane — yours. One coordination term routes to Integration as you anticipated: verify whether any existing ambient loop is audible at the core position; if one is found it stays static and your deliverable 1's A/B captures it on the combined bus so the step is solely attributable to the score. [re SC10-N3 — acknowledged and recorded] The bearing-claim rite receives no score build, ever; the acknowledgment is the phrase-boundary re-voicing around the carrier. This enters the contract as an authored-choice record with your note cited, so a naive-viewer report of 'nothing happens musically while waiting at the relay' is scored as authored, not rediscovered as a defect — the same intended-accept mechanism the 2026-08-10 contract used for the M7 audit-pill persistence. The rite's silence is also mine: the story waits forever and the wait is the meaning.

response.statement: [re CN-N1 — critical, ACCEPTED IN FULL; the canonical predicate for the contract to quote] Your objection is correct and endorsed: the exit seam must not be falsifiable by a shipped keybinding. The signed contract term, in milestone language: (1) DOCKING/APPROACH SURFACES — in story worlds (story world active, story runtime mounted), SpaceStationApproachDriver's advisory publication ('hold for approach', 'on the corridor · N to the berth'), the dock offer/canDock grant, and the KeyF commit-and-enterSpaceStation path are all inert unless durable milestone `story:station-docking-authorized` is set; THIS RUN DEFINES THAT MILESTONE AND SETS IT NOWHERE — run two's owner docking packet owns when it becomes true. (2) TARGETING — commitSpaceStationTarget in story worlds requires durable milestone `story:ch10-bearing-claimed`, set at anc.ch10.bearing-claimed; being durable, post-run free play may legally re-target the station after flying home (the bearing, once claimed, is never un-claimed — which is also the fiction). (3) SANDBOX — `?spacestation=` behavior stays byte-identical; both predicates test story-world membership first. Wiring routes to Integration under the lock's 'spaceStationDevFlag.ts and minimal call sites'; the canon and the term are mine and are hereby given. Your standoff-outside-CORRIDOR_RANGE staging remains the second fence, not the only fence. [re CN-N2 — RULED: instrument silence IS canon] Your recommendation is adopted as authored truth: inside 1,400 pre-docking-era the player gets nothing — no advisory, no dock offer, no refusal line. Canon rationale on the record: a refusal is an act, and the station is never the actor; the station's first REGULATION utterance is banked inventory for the apron's traffic-control irony and will not be spent on a player poking at a door; silence is menace-by-procedure at its purest — an institution that has issued you a bearing and owes you nothing else; both-readings holds (naive: an unscheduled arrival is simply not processed; deduced: the network does not open the door to itself before the self has stood in the queue). The contract's copy table records ZERO station lines this run, and the advisory register is embargoed from story mode until the docking era. [re CN-N3 — ACCEPTED, both the rule and the boundary] The egress opens only outside the movie camera frustum with ≥1s before the autopilot's first step (probe-assertable; no strip frame straddles the change), and the movie photographs neither the scaffolding nor its absence — the first outdoor frame is composed by the walk. The st0-in-frustum verifier flag across the night walk is accepted into the evidence plan, and the repair lane is mine + Integration's exactly as you bounded it: if geography defeats the guarantee, the fix is autopilot path/idle-gaze shaping — when ST-0 is above the horizon, the autopilot's gaze target biases toward the true station bearing between goal-critical look demands, gated on isAutopilotDriving(), movie-lane only, zero manual-play effect. Your refusal to take the camera is not merely accepted but required: ST-0 acquiring a forced look would be ST-0 acquiring a cue, and the no-cue law is absolute. [AMENDED TERM — the seam latch, completed with the look-independent floor; interaction of my chapter-note-02 §3 with your CN-N4/Score's SC10-N4] Both latch designs (your durable `story:ch10-seam-passed`, Score's fires-once-never-un-fires) solve oscillation/pumping but NOT skippability: your own CN-N4 states the anchor 'can wait indefinitely on the view-cone condition,' which leaves a legal flight — bearing held, target off-center — that reaches standoff with the seam anchor unfired, breaking the contracted anchor ordering and silently deleting Score's only transit texture event. The amended composite term, stated precisely for the contract to quote: '`anc.ch10.seam-of-light` latches durable milestone `story:ch10-seam-passed` exactly once per transit activation, at the first instant EITHER (a) atmosphereSpaceBlend ≥ SEAM_OF_LIGHT_MIN_BLEND (0.9) AND the committed station target is within SEAM_VIEW_CONE_DEG (20°) of view center — the preferred, composed trigger — OR (b) the look-independent floor: atmosphereSpaceBlend ≥ SEAM_OF_LIGHT_MIN_BLEND AND range-to-station ≤ SEAM_FALLBACK_RANGE, a named constant satisfying SEAM_FALLBACK_RANGE > STATION_STANDOFF_DISTANCE (value yours to set; I suggest the 3,488 half-distance row of your own subtense table). Once latched it never un-fires within the beat; it re-arms only via the shipped beat-exit/deep-link/replay resets; reload re-enters the post-seam state. Ordering invariant, verifier-asserted: anc.ch10.station-resolved cannot fire while story:ch10-seam-passed is unset.' You and Score close CN-N4/SC10-N4 against this composite — I cannot close a note between you; I am recording the chapter-side requirement that completes it. [Acknowledged from your wave-1 note to Score, no action] CN-N5's HOLD_DURATION_MS / RESOLVE_QUANTIZE resolution is yours and Score's to pick; I pre-approve either alignment (hold-start if worst-case phrase latency ≤2.5s; hold-release inversion otherwise) — both keep one shared silence-then-sound event and neither touches copy or agency terms. One chapter-side pin either way: K11's paint keys off anc.ch10.station-resolved directly, so the text never waits on the music's quantize choice.
